foundation: Barrot V3 remains the execution, security, preservation and verification foundation.

latest_located_account_snapshot.limitation: The rich-list page reports a rounded 233.5M XRP balance at a validated ledger closed 21:59 UTC. It does not expose outbound count or trustline state in the ranked table. The earlier 20:00 UTC XRPLDashboard snapshot reported 233,461,943.7 XRP and zero outbound transactions.

summary.conclusion: 233.46M native XRP left five Binance-attributed hot wallets and was consolidated into one new XRPL account. The latest located public snapshot reports no outbound movement through 2026-11-01 20:00 UTC. Native XRP was not issuer-frozen. Binance separately reported XRP customer balances 100% backed and included XRP in phase-one withdrawal reopening. Neither statement proves an XRP-specific buyback quantity or attacker sale.

account_observations.caveat: These snapshots support inactivity only through their stated cutoffs, not at the current handoff cutoff.

secondary_leads_not_yet_independently_re.claim: A 42,750,000.1 RLUSD payment attempted at 2026-10-29T20:04:52Z failed with tecNO_DST, eight seconds before the first XRP payment created the destination account.
secondary_leads_not_yet_independently_re.implication: If confirmed, this may indicate a common withdrawal instruction sequence. The failed transaction delivered no RLUSD.
secondary_leads_not_yet_independently_re.required_verification: Retrieve exact validated-ledger transaction hash, source, destination, delivered_amount and transaction result.

secondary_leads_not_yet_independently_re.claim: The receiving account had zero trustlines and therefore could not hold RLUSD or other issued assets at the reported snapshot.
secondary_leads_not_yet_independently_re.required_verification: Confirm AccountRoot and RippleState objects at a pinned ledger index.

attribution.trm_assessment: High confidence, based on on-chain and off-chain intelligence.
attribution.fbi_position: The FBI's 2026-10-31 public alert states North Korea was responsible for the theft of more than $6B from Binance and names the activity TraderTraitor.
attribution.caveat: Binance's completed technical postmortem was not located by this evidence cutoff.

technical_assessment.trm_assessment: The Ethereum leg used EIP-7702 delegation and pre-signed authorizations. Transfers from Binance wallets on the other nine chains were ordinary signed transfers. TRM assesses compromise of Binance hot-wallet signing infrastructure as the most likely explanation.
technical_assessment.xrpl_implication: The cited evidence does not identify an XRPL consensus, validator, cryptographic or protocol vulnerability. The XRP payments were validly signed transfers from Binance-attributed hot wallets.

actions.details: Approximately $823M in the main receiving wallet plus a later $1.56M freeze.
TRM reports 40.5M RLUSD remained when Ripple froze the relevant wallet at 22:01 UTC; 48M had already been sold through DEXs from the 88.5M stolen.

native_xrp.consequence: Recovery depends on subsequent movement, tracing, exchange/bridge screening, legal process or voluntary return. Issuer freeze controls for stablecoins do not apply to native XRP.

freeze_and_control_asymmetry.caveat: A frozen token is not necessarily recovered or returned to Binance. Values are TRM's incident-time chain-analysis snapshot, not final recovery accounting.

company_claims: Phase-one withdrawal reopening was scheduled for 06:00–09:00 UTC on November 1 and explicitly included XRP on the XRP Ledger.
Binance stated BTC, ETH, USDT, BNB, SOL, USDC, XRP, USD1, RLUSD and ZEC customer balances were 100% backed.
Binance reported approximately 95% of the total incident amount covered, up from 90%.
The remaining 5% consisted of assets outside the listed top ten and was being sourced through market and OTC channels.
Binance said it would bear the financial impact rather than pass it to users.
limitations: The 95% figure is aggregate across affected assets, not an XRP-specific replenishment percentage.
The 100% XRP backing statement does not disclose whether replacement came from treasury inventory, internal transfers, market purchases, OTC purchases or a combination.
No XRP-specific acquisition quantity, execution venue, timestamp or counterparty has been verified.
The official announcement schedules phase-one reopening; an independent successful XRP withdrawal test was not performed.
market_interpretation: The theft transfer itself does not establish a market sale.
An XRP reserve replacement creates external spot/OTC demand only to the extent it requires net acquisition rather than internal inventory transfers.
Withdrawal suspension and phased reopening can affect venue liquidity, customer confidence and exchange-specific balances independently of XRP's global supply.

Harvest's ledger 108053752 balance-only observation at 2026-11-01T21:59Z reports approximately 233.5M XRP, consistent with XRPLDashboard's exact 233,461,943.7 XRP at 20:00Z. The later source confirms balance magnitude but not inactivity.
limitations: These are not four independent investigations of attacker identity; most XRP amount evidence derives from the same public ledger events.
Exchange-wallet labels are third-party attribution, not protocol-level identity proof.
Binance reserve/replenishment claims are company statements; independent reserve reconciliation was not completed.
The latest located recipient-account snapshot is November 1 20:00 UTC, not this handoff cutoff.
Harvest's 21:59Z rich-list snapshot is the latest located balance observation; it is not a current 2026-11-02 pinned-ledger query and does not establish zero outbound transactions after 20:00Z.

causal_hypotheses.thesis: The stolen XRP was consolidated into one receiving account and remained unmoved through the latest located November 1 snapshot; the transfer itself does not demonstrate a market sale.
disconfirming_evidence: Future movement or off-ledger monetization could change the assessment.
missing_data: Current AccountRoot and transaction history at a pinned validated ledger.
Subsequent DEX, bridge or exchange-deposit interaction.

causal_hypotheses.thesis: Replacing the stolen XRP could create in-kind market/OTC demand if Binance lacked sufficient unencumbered XRP inventory.
supporting_evidence: Binance says affected assets were replenished and remaining assets were being sourced through market/OTC channels.
Binance reported XRP customer balances 100% backed.
disconfirming_evidence: Remaining 5% of aggregate incident amount was outside the listed top ten, which included XRP.
No XRP-specific purchase quantity, venue or execution timestamp disclosed.
Internal treasury inventory can restore backing without new spot demand.
missing_data: Before/after Binance XRP Proof-of-Reserves wallet balances.

causal_hypotheses.thesis: Native XRP cannot be issuer-frozen, unlike USDT, USDC, RLUSD and USD1, while stablecoin issuers and Arbitrum governance froze or removed substantial value.
supporting_evidence: No issuer-freeze mechanism for native XRP.
disconfirming_evidence: No issuer freeze does not make XRP untraceable or impossible to recover through exchange screening, legal process or voluntary return.
missing_data: Subsequent movement of the XRP account.
Any exchange/bridge screening or recovery announcement.

causal_hypotheses.thesis: The incident and withdrawal interruption may alter centralized-exchange liquidity, customer custody preferences, venue concentration and derivatives basis independently of XRP payment utility.
supporting_evidence: Binance suspended affected withdrawals and announced phased reopening.
The incident involved a large XRP hot-wallet balance and cross-chain signing infrastructure.
disconfirming_evidence: Binance stated XRP customer balances were fully backed and included XRP in phase-one reopening.
No synchronized venue-level order-book or customer-flow series is included here.
missing_data: Cross-venue order-book depth, basis, funding and OI before/after.

causal_hypotheses.thesis: The incident may be interpreted as an XRP Ledger security failure.
disconfirming_evidence: TRM says XRP payments were ordinary signed transfers from Binance wallets.
TRM points to Binance signing infrastructure across chains.
No cited evidence identifies an XRPL consensus or protocol vulnerability.

leakage_controls: Keep publication, observation and ingestion timestamps separate.
Do not backdate Binance statements to the incident timestamp.
Do not treat the November 1 account snapshot as known before its capture time.
Do not infer purchases from reserve-backing claims.
Do not count frozen stablecoins as recovered/returned.
Do not equate an exchange-wallet transfer with a market sale.

prediction_record.reason: The incident is a material event feature, but synchronized post-event price, venue-normalized liquidity, exchange withdrawal/replenishment flows and order-book data are unavailable. No calibrated out-of-sample XRP model skill has been established.
prohibited_claims: No claim Binance bought exactly 233.46M XRP.
No claim the attacker sold the XRP.
No claim XRPL itself was compromised.
No claim all frozen assets were recovered.

security_pr.limitation: Current-main security remediation remains inactive until an authorized proposal is merged.

repository_handoff.preservation: No main ref modification, merge, force-push, manual workflow dispatch, secret access, deployment, paper-position mutation or real-money trade.

root_cause: The evaluator compares each signal against a single current CoinGecko price when the signal is at least 24 hours old; it does not enforce one fixed horizon.
The exact outcome observation timestamp and source-price snapshot are not recorded.
The workflow runs on a daily schedule, so actual elapsed horizons vary.
Historical JSONL signal rows are rewritten with checked/correct/price_at_check fields.
The score is reduced to broad >60/<40/neutral thresholds; the result is not a calibrated probability score.
No baseline comparison, walk-forward protocol, uncertainty interval or calibration analysis is present.
legacy_accuracy_audit.interpretation: The 45.5% value is a legacy descriptive tally only. It must not be described as XRP prediction accuracy, model skill or a measured win rate.

correction: Stops the live-price request and variable-horizon scoring.
Makes the scheduled workflow read-only and artifact-only.
Publishes NOT_EVALUATED / NOT_COMPARABLE while preserving the legacy 1697/772/45.5% tally for audit.
Labels the fixed-horizon ledger IMPLEMENTED_NOT_POPULATED because no verified XRP forecasts and resolved outcomes exist.

legacy_accuracy_audit.current_main_effect: The misleading legacy tally remains in main until the proposal is approved and merged. No merge was performed.

platform_status.rule: No platform is described as collaborating live without authenticated, tested request/response evidence.

spot.timestamp_quality: Page crawled 2026-11-02; exact underlying quote timestamp not exposed.

caveats: October 30 is the first post-incident U.S. ETF session; the T+1 snapshot is partial because XRPZ and GXRP had not reported.
October 29 ETF flow was +$8.4M, but the Binance XRPL theft began at 20:05 UTC (4:05 p.m. ET), after the U.S. cash-session close; do not attribute the October 29 flow to the incident.
Cumulative net flows and fund AUM are different quantities; AUM includes price effects.

lagged_13f_institutional_holdings.caveat: Lagged Q2 2026 13F data; not a current holdings snapshot and excludes positions not reportable under 13F.

market_snapshot.admission_rule: Do not average these OI series. Venue, contract, quote-currency, aggregation and timestamp coverage differ materially. Long-account share is not notional exposure. Positive funding is not by itself a directional signal.
